scorecards.inningsCommentary: Zimbabwe commenced their first innings at Sylhet International Cricket Stadium, aiming to set an imposing baseline total. The centerpiece of the innings was a brilliant 88 from SC Williams, complemented by a commanding 72-run stand between PJ Moor and SC Williams that absorbed bowling hostility and accelerated the scoring rate to 2.4 RPO. Bangladesh's bowling response was spearheaded by Taijul Islam (6/108), who generated sustained pressure and triggered critical breakthroughs to prevent runaway scoring. Concluding at 282/10 (117.3 ov), Zimbabwe posted a competitive total, ensuring a closely matched contest.

Imrul Kayes anchored the innings with a resolute 43, providing backbone against a probing bowling attack while middle-order partnerships consolidated the position. Zimbabwe's bowling response was spearheaded by B Mavuta (4/21), who generated sustained pressure and triggered critical breakthroughs to prevent runaway scoring. Dismissed for 169/10 (63.1 ov), Bangladesh succumbed to fourth-innings pressure as Zimbabwe's bowlers closed out the victory.

summaryTab.matchStory: Zimbabwe recovered from early pressure in the first innings, anchored by SC Williams's resolute 88 to post 282. Bangladesh responded with 143 as both teams traded momentum in high-stakes middle sessions. Zimbabwe posted 181 in their second innings, shifting match momentum decisively through crucial partnerships. B Mavuta spearheaded Zimbabwe's attack to bowl out Bangladesh for 169 and seal victory.

summaryTab.matchCommentary:
The Test match at Sylhet International Cricket Stadium commenced with high tactical intensity as Zimbabwe posted 282/10 (117.3 ov) in their opening innings. In response, Bangladesh countered with 143/10 (50.6 ov), setting the stage for a compelling contest of tactical endurance. Early sessions tested batting resolve against disciplined seam movement, with both attacks striving to gain the upper hand on a developing surface.

The defining turning point arrived during 6-Wicket Spell: Taijul Islam (6/108), which irrevocably altered the trajectory of the match. As the match progressed through its pivotal middle stages, Taijul Islam delivered a masterclass for Bangladesh (8 Runs & 11 Wkts), absorbing intense pressure and tilting the momentum decisively. Crucial partnership stands and incisive bowling spells broke the opposition's resistance, shifting the control share (Zimbabwe 48%) and allowing Zimbabwe to dictate terms heading into the decisive sessions.

Entering the final innings, Bangladesh faced an uphill battle under unrelenting scoreboard pressure. Zimbabwe's bowling unit, bolstered by Sikandar Raza (44 Runs & 6 Wkts), maintained relentless discipline and attacked the stumps relentlessly. Wicket clusters in the closing sessions dismantled any remaining resistance, sealing Zimbabwe won by 151 runs in comprehensive fashion.

Verdict: Zimbabwe's triumph was built on superior pressure absorption, clinical execution during critical moments, and the ability to dominate key sessions. While Bangladesh produced fighting phases, Zimbabwe won the pivotal turning points and sustained higher tactical control across all five days to emerge as deserved victors.
